title: Can permission expire without forgetting?
question: When a learner explicitly authorizes Turtle to resurface retained context, how can that permission expire or be revoked cleanly while the underlying context remains returnable later?
why_now: The Resurfacing Authority Envelope separates relevance from permission. The next pressure point is whether valid learner-authored permission can stay bounded over time without becoming a permanent default or forcing deletion of useful retained context.
possible_possibles: A one-shot learner watchpoint that consumes itself after one authorized return.
A scope-and-time bounded resurfacing token the learner can inspect and revoke.
A quiet pull-tab history that stays returnable without maintaining active resurfacing permission.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — maybe the cleanest permission model is not a timer at all, but a little door the learner has to reopen each time.
constraints: Expiration or revocation must not erase the underlying learner-owned context.
Expired permission cannot be silently revived by relevance scoring.
Do not create person-wide defaults from a local authorization.
Human silence or availability must not be inferred as renewed permission.

ontology_mappings.rationale: Learners retain authority to grant, revoke, or let permission lapse.
Authority remains explicit and contestable rather than becoming a durable machine default.
Past permission cannot predetermine future resurfacing.
Context remains returnable through canonical pointers after permission expires.

ctc_mappings.rationale: The learner controls when prior inquiry re-enters the foreground.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: Permission state should be inspectable and revisable.
Return to prior material should be a deliberate reflective act.
Durable permission raises questions of power over attention and salience.

uncaptured_residue.observation: It is unresolved whether learners will prefer one-shot, timed, scope-bounded, or manually reopened resurfacing permission.
Formal revocability does not by itself guarantee that a resurfacing interaction feels non-pressuring.
